## M5 — The move repertoire

### M5.A The nine core moves

**M5.A.1** The core repertoire **MUST** be exactly: `PURSUE`, `DISTANCE`, `CONFLICT`, `OVERFUNCTION`, `UNDERFUNCTION`, `TRIANGLE`, `CUTOFF`, `I-POSITION`, `STAY-IN-CONTACT`. → §5.1

**M5.A.1a** — *each core move is a single act; the pattern of the same name is a readout.* `PURSUE`, `DISTANCE`, `CONFLICT`, `OVERFUNCTION`, `UNDERFUNCTION`, `TRIANGLE` and `CUTOFF` **MUST** each be one act on one tick: one approach, one withdrawal, one critical push, one instance of taking charge, one of giving way, one turn to a third person, one severing. The patterns Bowen named — conflict, over- and underfunctioning, distance, cutoff, projection, a fixed triangle — **MUST** be readouts over a tie's or a triangle's history of reciprocal acts, hardened by `M4.G.1`, and **MUST NOT** be selectable as units. "**Each of the three patterns solves the dilemma**… Each pattern solves it in a different way" (`kerr_book/ks04.md` · KS04.14): the patterns are solutions that substitute for one another, not acts. Each pattern readout's definition is `[I]` and **MUST** be declared before any criterion that reads it is run. → `model_explainer.md` §19 The owner gave the readouts' definitions on 2026-10-10 (`docs/readouts_phase_c.md`). A pattern is a **repeating** pattern of activity, 3 or more acts in 4 weeks, and it ends only when a new pattern emerges. No interaction is an emerging level of distance. Cutoff is rejection, not absence. Pursuit reads as fusion, over/underfunctioning or projection. Projection is declared as a readout now; its learning (`M4.D.6e`) stays Phase D. Cutoff read from behaviour (the owner: "The designation of cutoff emerges from behaviour. An agent saying 'I'm not going to contact you again' is not cutoff, it's just words that need behaviour to back it up"): member A's cutoff of B **MUST** be read from what A does — B's approaches refused (by the engine's refusal, `M1.B.3c`, or answered with `CUTOFF` or `DISTANCE`) at least `pattern_min_acts` times in the window, with no act with contact from A to B — and a `CUTOFF` act alone **MUST NOT** read as cutoff.

**M5.A.2** No move outside M5.A.1 and M5.B **MAY** be added without a citation in the explainer.

### M5.B The six the corpus adds

**M5.B.1** `DETRIANGLE` — return an aligned third party to neutral. **MUST** leave the third party's knowledge intact and change only their position. → `_RESOLUTIONS.md` R2

**M5.B.2** `PREVENT_ALIGNMENT` — act on *potential* alignment before it forms. **MUST** be available preemptively, not only in response to an alignment that has already occurred. → R2

**M5.B.3a** `REDUCE_CUTOFF` **MUST** have a **floor as well as no ceiling**, and the target is **one open relationship, not universality** — 1979 Tape 6 (T6.7): no one can have open relationships with everyone, but there is some indication that an open tie with those who matter most, even a single significant person, makes for healthier living. Cutoff is load-bearing for the person maintaining it — the KB05 interview calls cutting off a lifeline that allows someone to get by and adapt — so it may be reduced only as fast as that person can absorb, and the far side of a cutoff has its own state and its own willingness. Total openness is also not the target: the KB08 interview, while recommending near-complete disclosure between spouses as a workable exercise, says that keeping a self seems to require holding some of it back from the other, and that if everyone in a family told everything, one person would lose self to the family as a whole. With `L12.4`'s two-sided closeness band, four sources agree that **contact is not monotonically good**. → `kb/kb05.md` · K05.2, `kb/kb08.md` · K08.4

**M5.B.3** `REDUCE_CUTOFF` — increase contact on a severed tie (on a tie where either side holds `rejection`, `M1.B.3c`; it lowers the actor's own rejection, and contact the cutter accepts lowers theirs; it moves none of the tie's held anxiety, which contact bridges, `M1.D.2b`). **MUST** lower anxiety and **MUST NOT** directly raise `basic_level`. There **MUST NOT** be an optimum contact rate; more contact **MUST NOT** be penalised. → §5.7, §13.2. Reconciling with `M5.B.3a`: more contact on a severed tie is never penalised **as contact**, but it can carry the receiver past its optimum on the impingement side (`M4.C.1`), which is `M5.B.3a`'s bound. The transient cost **MUST** land on a third party whose distancing mechanism is being stripped, not on the person increasing contact (`L22.6`, external review G1) — as the **loss of that outlet**, not as a transfer of the tie's held anxiety (the owner's D7, 2026-10-19): the expected route is triangle position, the third party becoming the outsider of the triangle holding the tie (`M1.C.1`). Not yet shown: `tests/bowen/test_cutoff_stock.py::test_m5b3_third_party_cost_is_the_lost_outlet` compares the children's anxiety after a scripted bridging with the tie left cut, over 8 seeds, and found no rise; it is a strict expected failure, and no cost is written to make it pass.

**M5.B.4** Family→external moves `SPLIT`, `FRAME_AMBIGUITY`, `DISPLACE` **MUST** exist. `FRAME_AMBIGUITY` **MUST** capture the external agent's *silence* as carrying professional weight — abstention **MUST NOT** be an exit. → §5.7

**M5.B.6** `PROVOKE` — raise an issue deliberately, at low stakes. Its intensity **MUST** be a dial separate from its content, and it is the move by which `M5.C.1a`'s peace-agree technique raises an old issue and the live-issue gate (`M5.C`) is met. → `model_explainer.md` §5.7; `L21.6`, `L21.9`

**M5.B.5** The external agent's repertoire **MUST** be a strict subset: `STAY-IN-CONTACT`, `I-POSITION`, `OVERFUNCTION`, `TRIANGLE`, `CUTOFF`, plus M1.E.3 and M1.E.4. → §5.8

### M5.C Gates

**M5.C.1** Each gate below **MUST** be evaluated before selection and **MUST** be able to remove a move from the draw.

| Gate | Effect | Explainer |
|---|---|---|
| `outside_ness` below threshold | `I-POSITION` lands as empty words or an assault — **not** as a weakened success. Two thresholds, one per axis of `M1.A.9a`, both `[I]`; the gate fails on either | §5.3 |
| `financially_dependent` | `I-POSITION` **MUST** fail outright | §3.12 |
| no live issue | `I-POSITION` **delayed**, **MUST NOT** be blocked | §5.3 |
| mover's own engagement too high | `I-POSITION` backfires, with a long recovery cost on that tie | §5.3 |
| system calm | triangles inoperative; projection **MUST NOT** fire. The triangle clause is superseded by amended `M1.C.3` and is not a gate; the projection clause is Phase D (`M4.B.2a`) | §5.3 |
| marital distance high | any move targeting the symptom-bearer **MUST** produce no improvement. While both spouses' felt contact on the family's marital tie is below `marital_distance_fraction` (0.25, `[I]`) of their optimum, a move addressed to one of the couple's children with an active symptom cannot lower their acute anxiety, and no calm transfer (`M4.C.10`) reaches them (a symptomatic spouse is not gated); engine-side, so it reads the tie's true state | §5.3 |
| decision ownership held externally | removal **MUST NOT** fire even at tolerance | §5.3 |

**M5.C.1a** — *the live-issue gate MUST carry a family-type term, and this is a SAFETY property.* For a **peace-agree** family, which erases its differences fast, an old issue is deliberately raised to produce workable reactivity. For a **reactive, explosive** family the technique **inverts**: calm self first, and the success criterion is **relative** — the KB06 interview says one need not control one's reactiveness completely; being less reactive than everyone else present is already a step toward a calmer family (`kb/kb06.md` · K06.4).
Applying the peace-agree technique to a reactive family is not merely ineffective. `KB08` records three outcomes of forcing conjoint contact on families already at capacity: acute psychosis; a young woman, severely disturbed, who by a second-hand account from the early days blinded herself after a young therapist insisted on whole-family meetings; and a patient who, two weeks into a study of joint meetings the family had been warned it probably could not bear, took her life while on leave from the hospital. → `kb/kb05.md` · K05.1, `kb/kb06.md` · K06.4, `kb/kb08.md` · K08.1

**M5.C.2** — *the non-monotonicity is on the mover's axis.* `I-POSITION` **MUST NOT** be gated on mid-band *family* anxiety. High-anxiety family events — serious illness, death — **MUST** be enabling. What backfires is the mover's own engagement level. An implementation that suppresses the move at high family anxiety is a failing implementation. → §5.3

### M5.D `I-POSITION` is a state machine

**M5.D.1** `I-POSITION` **MUST NOT** be a single-tick move with a propensity.

**M5.D.2** States, in order: `PREPARE` → `DEFINE` → `OPPOSITION` → (`ABORT` | `HOLD`) → `PEAK` → `RESOLVE` → `FOLLOW_UP`.

**M5.D.2a** — *`PREPARE` **MUST** exist and **MUST** be able to fail.* A differentiating move is not emitted on the tick it is decided. Bowen's own February 1967 effort ran **months of planning** and **one private letter per important triangle**, timed "**to cause the triangles to come to me.**" `PREPARE` therefore **MUST** occupy multiple fast ticks, **MUST** be able to act on each triangle separately (M5.B's `PREVENT_ALIGNMENT`), and a sequence entering `DEFINE` without it **MUST** carry a lower probability of reaching `PEAK`. This is also where M5.D.8's "several failures" partly lives: an unprepared move is one of the ways an attempt fails. → `theory/family_evaluation/fe11.md` · FE11.9

**M5.D.3** The abort branches — defend, counterattack, go silent — **MUST** sit at the *first* opposition and **MUST** be the usual outcome, not an exception. Each **MUST** return the mover to the prior balance.

**M5.D.4** The **mover's freedom from anger MUST** be the gate admitting the sequence to `PEAK`. Ch13 mentions anger once and only once, and it is the mover's: "When he is finally able to maintain his course **without getting angry at the opposition**, the opposition does a final intense emotional attack. If he remains calm with this, the opposition becomes calm and pulls up to his level of individuality." An angry mover **MUST** therefore **stall** the sequence — the final attack does not come at all — rather than abort it loudly. Anger **MUST NOT** be implemented as a fourth abort branch **and MUST NOT** be implemented as the condition that admits the peak. → `theory/ch13.md` · verified against the primary chapter, 2026-08-27

**M5.D.4a** — *the mover's anger MUST degrade the move, not merely delay it.* `I-POSITION` emitted while the mover's own anger is above threshold **MUST** execute as `M5.F.4`'s assertion form and **MUST** count as negative evidence under `M5.F.2a`. The gate **MUST** be read when the act is selected and again when a sequence's `DEFINE` is said: a mover angry then says the position as the assertion form, all demand, and the sequence ends there, with no opposition and the tie's balance not restored, since the position was said. **Two** statements about the **mover's** anger, from two authors two decades apart — plus a third that corroborates only the dogmatism half. *Corrected 2026-08-28: the requirement claimed all three were about anger. Bowen's sentence says nothing about anger, a mover, or an I-position; it sits in a passage on Georgetown trainee selection.* Ch13 above; Kerr 1988 — "**it is not fueled by anger. Anger can sometimes be a stimulus to clarify one's thinking, but it is not a reliable guide for action. When someone angrily and dogmatically claims to be a 'self,' he is usually unsure of his position and is blaming others for his plight in life**"; and Bowen 1988, written independently in the same volume — "**A dogmatic person is rarely sure of self.**"
**What anger is, in this model.** Not a gate and not a state (M1.A.0 still binds): an **intensity level on the negative side of the appraisal**, whose *handling* is the differentiation readout — noticed and managed, or discharged reactively as defence. The abort branches of M5.D.3 are what discharging it looks like. → *decision A3, 2026-08-27*; `theory/family_evaluation/fe04.md` · FE04.4, `fe11.md` · FE11.19

**M5.D.5** On a held `PEAK`, the opposition **MUST** pull up **to the mover's level**, not to a group mean, and the payoff **MUST** propagate to subsequent movers. Both parties rise, so the gain is **solid self**, which `M6.I.5` exempts from `M6.I.4`'s zero-sum exchange.

**M5.D.6** `FOLLOW_UP` **MUST** be mandatory on the next day *relative to the resolving encounter*. Skipping it **MUST** revert the gain. "The next day" is **the fast tick after `RESOLVE`** — the tick is a week (`M3.A.1`) and latency is whole ticks (`M3.C.2`). Sub-week durations in the explainer are not calibration targets.

**M5.D.9** — *a sequence that spans ticks, and one outcome per tick.* While a person is in an `I-POSITION` sequence, a tick on which a sequence step is due **MUST** resolve to that step (`M4.D.1`); on any other tick the person selects normally, and acts on the sequence's tie count as `STAY-IN-CONTACT`. A step that collides with a forced outcome (`M4.D.1f`) **MUST** be deferred one tick and logged.

**M5.D.7** Only a sequence reaching `FOLLOW_UP` counts as a *completed* exchange. A completed exchange **MUST** raise `functional_level` and **MUST** trigger the triangle decrement (M1.C.5). It **MUST NOT** write `basic_level`, which is derived (M1.A.4a) and reachable only through sustained, broad functional improvement.

**M5.D.7a** The `functional_level` increment **MUST** be small enough, and M1.A.4a's window and breadth requirements strict enough, that no realistic number of completed exchanges moves an agent materially up the `basic_level` scale within a run. The config **MUST** carry a comment saying why. Bowen names the contrary reading as the field's characteristic misconception: in the KB01 interview he calls it grotesque that people treat differentiation as something finished in a weekend, or even an hour. *Corrected 2026-08-28; paraphrased at SP-1 (ASR rule). KB01's Otter transcript labels the speaker, so the attribution to Bowen stands.* Ch21's trip is **one step in a decades-long effort**, not the unit of differentiation.

**M5.D.7b** A readout **MUST NOT** describe an agent that has completed an `I-POSITION` sequence as *differentiated*, or report completed exchanges as a differentiation score. → `theory/_KERR_INTERVIEWS.md`

**M5.D.8** Success **MUST** usually follow several failures. An implementation in which the first attempt typically succeeds is a failing implementation.

### M5.E The reaction ladder

**M5.E.0** — *revision 11: the ladder is learned.* `M5.E.1`–`M5.E.6` describe the shape the system's reaction takes. That shape **MUST** be produced by the other members' automatic-channel learning in response to `M5.E.7`'s debit — the mover withdraws energy they were receiving, pressure that restores it relieves them, and `M4.D.6` reinforces the pressure — and **MUST NOT** be implemented as a scripted sequence of rungs. `M5.E.1`–`M5.E.6` are assertions for `M11.C.5`, not mechanisms.

**M5.E.1** The system response **MUST** run: *"You are wrong"* → *"Change back"* → *"If you do not, these are the consequences"*.

**M5.E.2** The reaction **MUST** decay unless fed by the mover defending or counterattacking.

**M5.E.3** Absence of any reaction **MUST** be interpreted as *the move did not land*, and **MUST NOT** be interpreted as success.

**M5.E.4** The ladder **MUST** admit a symptom rung at its foot — a symptom, not a verbal challenge, as the opening response — and a success branch at its head (the petition for sickness, which succeeds).

**M5.E.5** The push-back **MUST** be able to surface as symptom in a **third person**, not only as tension on the acting tie.

**M5.E.6** The trajectory **MUST** be a damped oscillation with hysteresis, not a spike-and-settle. Reversion **MUST NOT** be treated as run failure. → §8

**M5.E.7** The cause of the reaction **MUST** be the life-energy debit (M1.A.10, M6.I.3) — the move withdraws energy the other was receiving. The ladder is the surface expression. → §3.7

**M5.E.7a** — *what the debit **means** to the party who bears it.* The reaction occurs because the move **pushes the other to function more responsibly**, which they initially resist. The debit and the demand are one event seen from two ends, and stating it this way connects the change-back ladder to `M12`'s counterfeit of responsibility, which it otherwise touches nowhere. → user, A7 verdict 2026-08-24

**M5.E.8** — *the success state.* `M5.E` **MUST** have a terminal state that is **not** a return to baseline. A completed differentiating exchange **MUST** leave the tie **more solid** than before, with increased mutual respect — "**A hallmark of a successful effort to define 'self' is that it does not disrupt a relationship but, rather, solidifies it.**" `M11.C.5` **MUST** assert it. → `kerr_book/ks00.md` · KS00.6
Observed form: the pursue/distance polarity can **invert** — after a successful sequence, the previously pursuing party distances and the previously distancing party pursues (`ks17.md` · KS17.11). That inversion is assertable.

**M5.E.9** — *three timescales, and they are not one.* The config **MUST** declare all three separately, each `[I]` where the corpus gives no figure:

| Scale | What settles | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **~1 week** | the acute reaction at peak, before it breaks | `ks07.md` · KS07.1 |
| **months** | the system's re-equilibration after a held position | user, A7 verdict |
| **years to a decade** | resolution of a primary tie; **ten years** on one relationship, **twelve** of preparation for one visit | `ks00.md` · KS00.6; `ks15.md` · KS15.6 |

Together these bound `M5.D.7a`: **the unit of differentiation is not the exchange**, and no realistic number of exchanges moves an agent materially within a run.

### M5.F Act identity — the counterfeit problem

**M5.F.1** A move's effect **MUST NOT** be a function of move type and tie state alone. It **MUST** be multiplied by a hidden actor state (`outside_ness`) that receivers can read and the actor may not. Receivers "read" it only through the event — the actor's `outside_ness` scales the impingement component the event delivers (`M4.C.1`) — and **MUST NOT** read the field itself (`M4.B.2a`). That state is **two-dimensional** per M1.A.9a — outward impingement and inward impingement — and a scalar implementation is a failing implementation. → §5.6

**M5.F.2** The same move type at low `outside_ness` **MUST** be able to produce the *opposite* sign of effect, not merely a smaller one.

**M5.F.2c** — *the flip is gradual.* The sign change of `M5.F.2` **MUST NOT** be a step. A move's effect **MUST** scale continuously with the actor's `outside_ness` on each axis, crossing zero at a declared point per axis, `[I]`, set at 0.5 for both. `I-POSITION`'s form follows the same rule: its demand share scales continuously with the mover's self-channel weight (`M5.F.4`), and no threshold on systems perspective decides it. The anger gate (`M5.D.4a`) is the one step left: it decides whether a sequence runs and, when a sequence's `DEFINE` is said, whether the position is said all as demand; below it the share is continuous.

**M5.F.2a** — *asserting a differentiated state MUST be negative evidence for it.* Five independent forms across five interviews: the KB04 interview treats telling someone that one will keep out of their problem as itself a sign of being involved (`KB04` · K04.10); the KB03 interview calls a therapist's announcement that the trouble is the family's alone largely denial, since the therapist is involved (`KB03` · K03.3); the KB06 interview takes a claim to have settled one's attachment to one's parents as evidence of that attachment, likely the more so as the claim is pressed harder (`KB06` · K06.7); the KB12 interview describes a poorly differentiated person's I-position as self-centred, dogmatic and overbearing (`KB12` · K12.3); and the KB07 interview counts catching oneself diagnosing, criticising or praising someone as a lapse in systems perspective (`KB07` · K07.1). → `kb/_KB_PASS2.md`
**Consequence:** a cheap readout computable from the event log, and the discriminator M5.F.3 asks for. An agent that announces its own neutrality **MUST** score lower on `outside_ness`, not higher.

**M5.F.2b** The counterfeit detector **MUST** report **which axis failed** (M1.A.9a). A single scalar score is a failing implementation, because the forceful declarer and the compliant accommodator are counterfeits in **opposite** directions and require opposite corrections. → M11.C.19

**M5.F.4** — *the lower the mover's level, the more an `I-POSITION` comes out as a demand.* A genuine `I-POSITION` — the `DEFINE` event of `M5.D`'s sequence — **MUST** be a mixture of a self-statement, share `w`, and a demand, share `1 − w`, where `w` is the mover's own self-channel weight that week (`M4.D.1a`: `w = f + perspective_channel_gain × perspective × (1 − f)`, `f = (functional_level ÷ 100)^self_channel_exponent`). The demand share **MUST** add `(1 − w) × assertion_gain` to the impingement the event delivers (`M4.C.1`), so it raises reactivity on the tie; the debit of the target's felt contact (`M5.E.7`) **MUST** be scaled by `w`; and the mover's outward axis **MUST** rise by `(1 − w) × assertion_evidence_gain`, negative evidence under `M5.F.2a`. The **assertion form** is the mixture at `w = 0` — the full `assertion_gain`, no debit, the full `assertion_evidence_gain` — and an angry mover's `I-POSITION` executes as it at once, with no sequence; a mover angry when a sequence reaches `DEFINE` says it as it, and the sequence ends (`M5.D.4a`, revision 41). No threshold on systems perspective decides the form: perspective enters through `w` alone, so a mover without it starts a sequence like any other (`M5.D.2a`) and, at `DEFINE`, says it mostly as a demand. At perspective 1, `w` is about 0.58 at level 40 and 0.68 at level 60; at perspective 0, 0.16 and 0.36. This keeps pseudo-differentiation an **output** of the model rather than a case the model must be told about separately. A poorly differentiated person can take an I-position, but a self-centred, dogmatic and overbearing one, and how it is taken reveals the level (the KB12 interview, `K12.3`, `[T]`); less differentiated people tend to take reactive I-positions that polarize the system and intensify anxiety (`KS05.5`, `[K]` `[T]`); an effective I-position defines what the person will do, not what others should do (`KS06.11`, `[K]` `[T]`); many so-called I-positions are attempts to get others to change or to pry oneself loose from emotionally intense situations (`FE04.13`, `[K]` `[T]`). The demand share models the first kind only; the second is not modelled, since no source gives it a size and it would need a motive the agents do not carry. That the demand share falls as level rises is the direction those passages give (`[K]` `[D]`, with the KB12 interview); the mixture, `w` as its share, and the three terms it scales are the model's (`[M]` `[I]`). `L10.12` and `FE11.19` (`[B]`) support the dogmatic form, not a gradient by level. No new constant; `assertion_perspective_threshold` is retired from the register. → `M4.D.1a`, `M5.D.4a`, `M5.E.7`, `M5.F.2a`, `M5.F.2c`, `M11.C.49`

**M5.F.5** The self-directed channel's objective (M4.D.1a) **MUST** be the two-axis position of M1.A.9a — both impingement axes low — and **MUST NOT** be discomfort reduction. A differentiated move is held **through** discomfort; scoring it by the actor's own relief reproduces M4.D.6a's forbidden proxy at the objective level. That signal is not forbidden in the automatic channel, but it is forbidden here: the self-directed channel **MUST NOT** be scored by relief.

**M5.F.3** Concession **MUST** be gradable continuously by the receiver, not as a binary. → §5.6
